Please apply to this job if you have the qualifications.  Every qualified American applicant helps deny a Green Card to an H1B trying to change status.

Duties: Design digital and print communications for our platform,  website, and social media, ensuring concepts work globally while scaling  effectively for local needs. Collaborate with brand, marketing,  content, and product design teams to translate business and marketing  strategies into visually compelling artwork across all media channels.  Create high-fidelity visuals, polished interaction prototypes, video and  motion-graphics style frames, exhibition graphics, print collateral,  presentations, infographics, branding assets, and digital  advertisements. Develop beautiful, thoughtful, and engaging website  experiences for all digital properties, and drive continuous iteration  on existing sites. Apply deep knowledge of design systems and scalable  design patterns, ensuring consistency and efficiency across all creative  output. Help design for complex projects, advocating for visual  excellence, user-centered design principles, and brand consistency  throughout the entire creative process. Drive a collaborative and  communicative workflow—from early-stage concepting and mood-boarding  through final visual execution. Work closely with cross-functional  partners including designers, product managers, software engineers,  strategists, and executives to deliver high-impact creative solutions.  Provide constructive, actionable feedback to design and writing peers to  elevate overall team quality. Support the fast-moving creative needs of  editorial, content, and social marketing teams with agility and  attention to detail. Partner with product managers and product designers  to create thoughtful icons, illustrations, and visual elements for our  products and platform. Conduct independent creative research to generate  insights and inspiration for innovative design ideas. Uphold and expand  upon existing brand and campaign systems to ensure strong, cohesive  visual identity across all touchpoints.

Requires a Bachelor's degree in Graphic Design, Computer Arts or a  related field plus 2 years of experience in a related occupation.  Requires 2 years of experience (or knowledge of with a Master's) in the  following: Cross-Functional Collaboration: partnering with product  designers, PMs, developers, and marketing teams to deliver cohesive,  scalable design solutions; Design System Development: integrating  visual/motion into design systems, contributing visual/animation  specifications, and ensuring scalability and consistency across  components; Visual and Motion Design Systems & Principles: defining,  implementing, and maintaining visual/motion design guidelines that  improve usability, accessibility, and brand storytelling across digital  experiences; Prototyping, Visual & Animation Tools: After Effects,  Rive, Lottie, Figma, and 3D design/animation tools for creating  high-quality visual/motion and interaction prototypes; Interaction &  UX Integration: user experience principles, with the ability to apply  visual/motion purposefully to enhance clarity, hierarchy, and user  engagement. Also requires 1 year of experience (or knowledge of with a  Master's) in Creative Direction & Mentorship. Alternatively,  employer will accept a Master's degree in Graphic Design, Computer Arts  or a related field plus knowledge of the above detailed skillsets.  Telecommuting (remote work) is permitted.

To apply: Visit https://t.co/l37dAw7Yk1

Learning in 2026 means adapting fast.

The way we learn is changing, so before diving into a new skill it’s worth asking yourself whether you want to learn it the traditional way.

I’ve been exploring AI tools to add motion and animation to my UI designs, and so far, @figma Make has impressed me the most. It’s still in beta, but it has consistently delivered me animations that feel close to what I had in mind and I'm very excited to see how this will develop in the future

@pizzaboy you done this with figma motion?
when i tried text animation like this it was painful as it split each letter into its own text field :/

Figma just launched Motion - native AI-powered animation built into the canvas. Keyframes, spring physics, bezier curves, AI-generated motion. No more Principle, Protopie, or After Effects for most design teams. https://t.co/cFpfJgAK24

@figma @kellaywho Pairing agent-generated motion with manual keyframe control in the same file is the piece most AI animation tools get wrong — you get something close, then can't fine-tune easing after. Commenting directly on motion prototypes should kill a lot of "check the Loom" handoffs too.
@pizzaboy Nice and booked, love to see it! Also the animation and sounds are great. Still need to give Figma motion a try.
